description: 48-question interview export mapping. Answers are Class 3 evidence leads, never scores.

questions.prompt: If I asked you to point at the landing-zone root today — tenant, organization or management account — what would you point at, and who owns it?
questions.hint: Explore named owners, extra directories, partner or acquisition clouds, and whether production exists outside the declared root. Distinguish the commercial payer from the technical organization.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: tenant/org ID, hierarchy export, billing-account mapping, named platform owner.

questions.prompt: What cloud estates, billing relationships or directories exist that are not on that map?
questions.hint: Explore leftover EA enrollments, personal tenants, standalone accounts, no-organization projects, sandbox clouds that grew up, and merged-company remnants.
questions.sample: Probe: “If finance forwarded last month’s invoices, would any of them surprise the platform team?”

questions.prompt: What actually runs in the management, payer or bootstrap plane?
questions.hint: Explore application workloads, data, developer sandboxes, and who has standing rights there. The management plane should host organization services, not business systems.
questions.sample: Ask them to list the last three resources created in that account — and who created them.

questions.prompt: How do billing, contract and technical ownership line up — and where do they disagree?
questions.hint: Explore invoice owners vs landing-zone owners, orphaned subscriptions, and cost allocation blocked by structure rather than tagging.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: billing export, enrollment/payer view, subscription-to-MG or account-to-OU map.

questions.prompt: If the person who can recover the cloud root left tomorrow, what would still work?
questions.hint: Explore break-glass, dual control, MFA on root/super-admin, where credentials live, and whether use would be noticed. Shared Global Admin or unused root keys are in scope.
questions.sample: Probe: “When was emergency access last tested — and who would see the log?”

questions.prompt: How do you know, this week, that you have a complete list of subscriptions, accounts or projects?
questions.hint: Explore API inventory vs spreadsheet vs workshop memory. New isolation units that first appear on an invoice are a finding.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: Resource Graph / Organizations / Asset Inventory export dated this week.

questions.prompt: How does a person get access to the cloud, and how is that access taken away?
questions.hint: Explore federation vs cloud-local users, shared logins, leaver processing, and whether IdP offboarding actually removes cloud rights.
questions.sample: Ask for the last leaver: what was revoked, by whom, and how would you prove it?

questions.prompt: How is privileged access granted, time-bounded, reviewed — and who still has it standing?
questions.hint: Explore PIM / Identity Center / PAM, approval, session length, Access Reviews, and standing Global Admin, AdministratorAccess or organizationAdmin on humans.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: eligible-role export, standing-assignment list, activation log, access review.

questions.prompt: How do workloads, pipelines and automation authenticate — without a person in the loop?
questions.hint: Explore managed identities, workload federation, IRSA, attached service accounts vs stored client secrets, IAM user keys and downloaded JSON keys.
questions.sample: Probe: “What would we find if we searched the CI variables for a cloud key?”

questions.prompt: Who has owner-equivalent rights at tenant, organization or management-group root, and why?
questions.hint: Explore app teams granted Owner ‘so they can work’, custom roles vs built-in Owner, and whether those grants can disable policy, logging or networking.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: role-assignment export at root / MG / org, SSO permission-set list.

questions.prompt: What is the break-glass path, who knows it, and would you know if it was used?
questions.hint: Explore dual control, exclusion from daily use, alerting, and whether emergency access is the unofficial admin account.
questions.sample: Probe: “Show me the alert that fires when break-glass signs in.”

questions.prompt: Where do local cloud users, shared mailboxes or long-lived keys still exist — and why have they survived?
questions.hint: Explore exceptions with owners and expiry vs tribal convenience. Capture the story; then ask what inventory would confirm it.
questions.sample: Ask for one ‘temporary’ key or user that is more than a year old.

questions.prompt: Walk me through the hierarchy. What does placing a workload in a given node actually change?
questions.hint: Explore management groups / OUs / folders as a policy spine vs a naming scheme. If moving a workload changes nothing, the hierarchy is a filing cabinet.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: hierarchy export, policy assignments per node, a recent move request.

questions.prompt: Where does the platform landing zone end and an application landing zone begin?
questions.hint: Explore identity, connectivity, logging, security vs application workloads. Listen for apps hosted in connectivity or management subscriptions.
questions.sample: Probe: “If we rebuilt the hub, which business systems would we have to migrate first?”

questions.prompt: How is a new subscription, account or project born — from request to ready?
questions.hint: Explore vending pipeline vs email-to-a-named-person vs portal click. Capture cycle time, who clicks, and what baseline is attached at birth.
questions.sample: Ask for the last three isolation units created and whether they landed in the right node with policy and logging on.

questions.prompt: How are naming and tags supposed to work — and what happens when they do not?
questions.hint: Explore documented standard vs create-time enforcement, untagged spend, and whether violations are noise or a ticket.
questions.sample: Probe: “Deploy something without the required tags. What stops you?”

questions.prompt: How are production and non-production kept apart — on paper, in IAM, and on the wire?
questions.hint: Explore shared subscriptions with ‘prod’ resource groups, shared admin roles, and playground identities that can reach production data.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: prod vs nonprod node, role assignments, peering / Shared VPC rules.

questions.prompt: What happens when someone creates a subscription, account or project in the portal outside the pattern?
questions.hint: Explore detection, follow-up, whether it is possible at all, and whether ClickOps is unofficially accepted.
questions.sample: Ask for a recent snowflake and whether it is still running.

questions.prompt: Where is the hub, and what is actually forced through it?
questions.hint: Explore hub-spoke / vWAN / TGW / Shared VPC, inspection placement, spoke-to-spoke defaults, and teams with their own internet edge.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: hub resource IDs, peering/attachment list, firewall policy, public-IP inventory.

questions.prompt: Who owns hybrid connectivity, and can an application team create a side door?
questions.hint: Explore ExpressRoute / Direct Connect / Interconnect / VPN landing in the platform vs in an app subscription. Redundancy and who-to-call belong here.
questions.sample: Probe: “Show me every circuit and VPN. Which of them did platform not approve?”

questions.prompt: How does a private name resolve in a new landing zone — including on-premises and private endpoints?
questions.hint: Explore central Private DNS / Route 53 Resolver / Cloud DNS vs per-team zones, hosts files, and ‘it works on my laptop’.
questions.sample: Ask them to resolve a private-endpoint name from a spoke that was vended last quarter.

questions.prompt: When is a public endpoint allowed, who approves it, and how does it die?
questions.hint: Explore deny policies vs honour system, public storage / K8s API / jump hosts, exception expiry, and whether a current public inventory exists.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: deny policy, public-IP/resource graph, exemption with owner and date.

questions.prompt: Can a non-production identity reach production on the network today?
questions.hint: Explore default spoke mesh, AllowVnetInbound, TGW default route tables, one big Shared VPC. Segmentation by naming is not segmentation.
questions.sample: Probe: “If a sandbox is compromised, what can it route to?”

questions.prompt: If we deleted the network slide deck, could you redraw the topology from inventory this week?
questions.hint: Explore whether peerings, attachments and interconnects have owners, and whether ‘temporary’ paths are still in production.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: peering/attachment export, undocumented ER authorizations, leftover VIFs.

questions.prompt: What does the landing zone actually stop a team from doing — not merely report after the fact?
questions.hint: Explore deny vs audit-only, MCSB / SCPs / org policies, and whether a new landing zone can boot with the baseline off.
questions.sample: Probe: “Create a public storage account in production. What happens?”

questions.prompt: Where do threat detections land, and who triages them with an SLA?
questions.hint: Explore Defender / GuardDuty / SCC at organization scope vs per-subscription islands, delegated admin, and findings nobody reads.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: org auto-enable, delegated security account, a finding ticket from last month.

questions.prompt: Where do keys and secrets actually live — vault, pipeline, wiki, or git?
questions.hint: Explore CMK claimed vs used, rotation, access logs, client secrets in CI, downloaded service-account keys, and secrets as identity.
questions.sample: Ask for one production secret’s home and its last rotation date.

questions.prompt: Where does security tooling live, and how do platform and SOC share a finding?
questions.hint: Explore a security landing zone vs marketplace products per team, RACI, and overlapping tools.
questions.sample: Probe: “A high-severity cloud finding arrives at 02:00. Who owns it?”

questions.prompt: When does security review happen relative to a workload going live?
questions.hint: Explore questionnaires after production, findings without a landing-zone owner, and ‘we’ll add Defender later’.
questions.sample: Ask for the last three go-lives and whether the baseline was already on.

questions.prompt: If an auditor asked for this week’s security posture of the landing zone, what would you export — not screenshot?
questions.hint: Explore Policy Insights / Config / SCC posture exports vs a dashboard PDF from last quarter.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: compliance export dated this week, with owners on non-compliant resources.

questions.prompt: Where do tenant, organization or account activity logs actually land, and for how long?
questions.hint: Explore org CloudTrail / MG diagnostic settings / org audit sinks vs logs left in the producing account at default retention.
questions.sample: Probe: “Could we reconstruct an admin action from 120 days ago without asking an app team?”

questions.prompt: When did you last export the live hierarchy, policy assignments and identity bindings?
questions.hint: Explore API-fresh inventory vs last year’s draw.io. Unknown isolation units discovered in a workshop are a finding.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: Resource Graph / Config aggregator / Asset Inventory taken for this assessment.

questions.prompt: What is monitored on the platform plane — logging pipeline, hybrid path, policy engine — not on the applications?
questions.hint: Explore whether a failed log export, dead ExpressRoute or deleted diagnostic setting would page anyone.
questions.sample: Ask who is on-call for the landing zone itself.

questions.prompt: If the landing zone burned down, what restores identity, DNS, policy, IaC state and keys?
questions.hint: Explore application backup (often mature) vs platform restore (often a laptop). Ask whether a restore has been rehearsed.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: state-backend location, Key Vault / KMS backup, last restore test date.

questions.prompt: How does the platform know what is running on the compute it hosts, and how is it updated?
questions.hint: Explore Update Manager / SSM / OS Config coverage, unmanaged images, and ‘we use Kubernetes so this does not apply’ as a claim to evidence.
questions.sample: Ask for agent coverage % and one fleet that is deliberately unmanaged.

questions.prompt: When was the last surprise — a missing account, a silent log gap, a platform alert that never fired?
questions.hint: This question is for tacit knowledge. Capture the story, then name the evidence that would have caught it.
questions.sample: Follow with: “What would we collect so the Engine can test whether that gap is still open?”

questions.prompt: Which guardrails are assigned at the hierarchy — and which still live only in a standard or a deck?
questions.hint: Explore MG/OU/folder assignments vs per-subscription cottage industry vs FullAWSAccess / empty initiatives / default org policies.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: effective policy on one production landing zone, assignment export.

questions.prompt: Name the small set of things the platform will not allow in production.
questions.hint: Public data, disable logging, leave the org, user-access-admin, any region, no tags. If the list is empty, prevention is goodwill.
questions.sample: Probe: “Which of those denies are in force on production, not only in a lab?”

questions.prompt: How is an exemption born, who owns it, and how does it die?
questions.hint: Explore expiresOn, review cadence, whole MGs/OUs excluded ‘for now’, and exemptions owned by a departed person.
questions.sample: Ask for the oldest production exemption and its expiry date.

questions.prompt: Can a team put a GPU farm in an unapproved region, untagged, with no budget owner?
questions.hint: Explore required tags, allowed locations, budgets. Cost reporting consumes these guardrails; it does not replace them.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: allowed-locations policy, required-tag policy, MG/account budgets.

questions.prompt: When you say the landing zone is compliant, what did you query — and when?
questions.hint: Explore Policy Insights / Config / SCC vs screenshots, questionnaires and workshop scores used as evidence.
questions.sample: Probe: “Show me non-compliant resources with owners, not a green tile.”

questions.prompt: Who can turn a deny into an allow at 2 a.m., and does the code catch up afterwards?
questions.hint: Explore portal exemptions during incidents, undocumented hotfixes, and whether the next pipeline run would surprise production.
questions.sample: Ask for the last emergency policy change and the follow-up PR.

questions.prompt: If we rebuilt the platform landing zones from the repository tomorrow, what would we get — and what would we miss?
questions.hint: Explore Terraform / Bicep / CDK / AFT / ALZ as system of record vs portal-first with exports after the fact.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: repo URL, last apply, plan vs reality, state-backend location.

questions.prompt: Walk through requesting a new landing zone or spoke. Who does the work, and how long does it take?
questions.hint: Explore catalog/pipeline vs email-request vs ticket-only. Self-service that nobody uses is still ticket-only.
questions.sample: Ask for request-to-ready time for the last five units, and whether the baseline was on at birth.

questions.prompt: How do you know when the cloud has left the code — and what happens then?
questions.hint: Explore drift detection, ignored drift, ‘apply would be destructive’, and recurring ClickOps offenders.
questions.sample: Probe: “When was the last drift signal, and did anyone act?”

questions.prompt: What can an application team get without a platform engineer performing the ritual?
questions.hint: Explore guardrailed self-service vs personality-based saying-no. Onboarding time dominated by platform wait is in scope.
questions.sample: Ask an application owner (if present) what they last waited on.

questions.prompt: Tell me about the last production hotfix to identity, hub, policy or logging.
questions.hint: Explore portal vs pipeline, break-glass record, whether code caught up, and whether the next apply is now unsafe.
questions.sample: Useful evidence leads: Activity Log / CloudTrail of the change, follow-up PR, or the absence of both.

questions.prompt: Which parts of the landing zone are still tribal knowledge — the steps that exist only in someone’s head?
questions.hint: This question is for silent knowledge. DNS, exemption ritual, vending exceptions, the ‘real’ network path. Capture names; then convert to evidence leads.
questions.sample: Follow with: “If that person is away for a month, what breaks — and what would we collect to make it visible to the Engine?”
